subject.title: [Feature]: sessions_kill should terminate all child exec processes spawned by a session

question: What public session exec-control contract and authorization boundary should OpenClaw expose for listing and terminating child exec processes spawned by a stored session?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear from source, but session-wide process visibility and termination can cross agent/session boundaries and must be a deliberate product and security choice before implementation.

options.title: Add guarded session exec control
options.body: Create additive Gateway and CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and tests for child, PTY, sandbox, and fallback behavior.

options.title: Extend existing session maintenance
options.body: Add explicit opt-in kill-exec flags to `sessions.abort` or `sessions.delete` while preserving current defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

options.title: Defer public operator surface
options.body: Keep only the existing agent-scoped process tool for now and handle restart/orphan cleanup in narrower lifecycle issues until a broader process-control design is ready.

recommendation.title: Add guarded session exec control
recommendation.body: Create additive Gateway and CLI methods for session exec list and kill with explicit operator scope, canonical session resolution, per-run outcomes, and tests for child, PTY, sandbox, and fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest available current blame and timeline signal across the Gateway session contract and process-control boundary.
